why: simple string with no escapes closes at the final quote
backslash-escaped quote stays inside the string; only the last quote closes it
doubled delimiter "" is a literal quote inside the string, not a close-then-reopen
an escaped backslash (even run) leaves the following real quote free to close the string
the literal ends at its own closing quote, not at the end of the whole source
an opening-bracket payload character must not be read as a real bracket
a quote payload character must not be read as a string delimiter
backslash-escape form for a named special character (newline)
backslash-escape form for an otherwise-unspecial payload character
the literal ends after its own payload character, not at the end of the whole source
